title: Arcane
body:
Arcane is a Docker management tool you host yourself. The README says "Modern Docker Management, Designed for Everyone."

The Starter plan of Portainer Business Edition is $1,045 a year. With Arcane you run it and keep it updated yourself.

A hundred people have contributed and the last commit was today. They moved feature requests to Discussions and issues are only for bugs now.
verdict: If you're fine running your own Docker tooling, you can cancel Portainer Business.

title: Dograh
body:
Dograh is an open source voice agent platform with a visual workflow builder. The README says you can self-host it with one Docker command. Vapi charges $29 a month for its Core plan.

It still costs money to run. You put in your own keys for the speech and language models and pay those providers directly, and you keep the server up yourself.

72 people have contributed to it and the last commit was yesterday.
verdict: If you don't mind running Docker and keeping your own API keys, you can cancel Vapi.

facts.description: Open source voice AI platform. Self-hosted alternative to Vapi and Retell. On Prem, BYOK across Speech to Speech or LLM/STT/TTS, with a visual workflow builder, MCP native and telephony support.

title: Hex
body: Wispr Flow Pro is $12 per user a month. Hex does the same thing on your own computer. You hold a key and talk, and the text gets pasted at your cursor in whatever app you have open. The first time you run it, it downloads a speech model, and after that the README says nothing leaves your machine. Twenty-five people have worked on it and the last commit was today.
verdict: If you mostly dictate into apps on your own desktop, you can cancel Wispr Flow.

facts.description: Local voice dictation for mac, windows and linux
facts.readme_excerpt: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History:     ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes wit
